newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banker Trust unit has plan for toxic site.
newsitem.headline: Banker Trust unit has plan for toxic site.

text.p: BT Funds Management Ltd said on Tuesday it had a strategy in place to bring about an environmental management plan for a contaminated property it owned in western Sydney.

The Rhodes property, near the Homebush Bay site for the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games, was the centre of controversy with environmental organisation Greenpeace claiming the site had become the "dioxin capital of the world".
Greenpeace said it had discovered drums of chemical storage on the site.

However, a spokesman for New South Wales environment minister Pam Allan said the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) was already aware of the situation and had acted accordingly to remedy the situation.
BT said it had been working with the EPA and the Office of Marine Administration and would happily comply with the EPA's storage recommendations.
BT said the soil had been deposited from an adjacent site, previously used by chemical giant Union Carbide, prior to BT's purchase.
